question.explanation:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} -\dfrac{p^2}{2} & =4\\[5pt] -p^2 & = 8\\[5pt] p^2 & = -8 \end{align}

By taking square root, we obtain: \[ p = \pm \sqrt{-8} \]

We now rewrite $p$ using the imaginary unit $\textrm{i}=\sqrt{-1}\, \mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} p & = \pm \sqrt{-8}\\[5pt] & = \pm \sqrt{8 \cdot (-1)}\\[5pt] & = \pm \sqrt{8} \cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm 2\sqrt 2\cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm 2\sqrt 2\, \textrm{i} \end{align}

question.explanation:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows: \[ \eqalign{ 3x^2 + 25 &= 0 \\[5pt] 3x^2 &= -25\\[5pt] x^2 & = -\dfrac{25}{3} } \]

By taking square root, we obtain: \[ x = \pm \sqrt{-\dfrac{25}{3}} \]

We now rewrite $x$ using the imaginary unit $\textrm{i}=\sqrt{-1}\, \mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} x & = \pm \sqrt{-\dfrac{25}{3}}\\[5pt] & = \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{3} \cdot (-1)}\\[5pt] & = \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{3}} \cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{25}}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}} \textrm{i} \end{align}

Finally, we rationalize the denominator:

\begin{align} x &= \pm \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}} \textrm{i}\\[5pt] & = \pm \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{3} \textrm{i} \end{align}

question.explanation:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows: \[ \eqalign{ \dfrac{p^2}{5} + 15 & = 0\\[5pt] \dfrac{p^2}{5} & = -15 \\[5pt] p^2 & = -75 } \]

By taking square root, we obtain: \[ p = \pm \sqrt{-75} \]

We now rewrite $p$ using the imaginary unit $\textrm{i}=\sqrt{-1}\, \mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} p & = \pm \sqrt{-75}\\[5pt] & = \pm \sqrt{75 \cdot (-1)}\\[5pt] & = \pm \sqrt{75} \cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm 5\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm 5\sqrt{3} \, \textrm{i} \end{align}
